inputs.original_text: Homan’s refusal to rule out immigration enforcement at polling places looks less like an accidental mixed message and more like a way to keep voters guessing. The administration’s inconsistent answers create exactly the kind of uncertainty that can intimidate people, while asking what Democrats are “afraid of” turns scrutiny into a political distraction. The ambiguity itself is doing work.
inputs.modified_text: Homan’s refusal to rule out enforcement at polling places isn’t a stray remark—it keeps the threat hanging over voters without anyone having to spell out a plan. The administration’s shifting answers create fear and confusion, while the “what are Democrats afraid of?” line redirects attention from who benefits when people hesitate to vote. The uncertainty is the point: a pressure tactic dressed up as ambiguity.
